mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (사업자등록증 / 법인등기사항전부증명서 equivalent) — Korean Registry Extract for the Newly Formed Chusik Hoesa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: Original Korean Certificate of Incorporation → Issuing court registry issuance → Notarization by Korean notary public (optional for court-issued certificates) → Apostille Certificate issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of the Republic of Korea → Present to overseas entity bank or foreign corporate registry without consular chain

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (법인등기사항일부증명서 / 국세완납증명) — Korean Corporate Registry Good Standing and Tax Payment Clearance Certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: Original certificate issued by Court Registry/NTS → Apostille by Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA) of the Republic of Korea → Direct submission to Hague member-state bank; for non-Hague states (e.g., UAE, China, Taiwan) use Consular Legalization path: Certificate → Korean MOFA certification → Consular Legalization at the Consular Office of the destination country in Korea → destination-country embassy/consulate legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney for Company Formation and Foreign Bank Account Opening (주식회사 설립 및 해외 계좌 개설 위임에 관한 이사회 결의)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: Board resolution signed by directors → Korean notary public notarization of corporate signatory authority → Apostille by MOFA Korea → use directly in a Hague member state; exchange control and bank compliance review by foreign bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (정관) — Certified True Copy of the Korean Stock Corporation Deed of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chusik Hoesa incorporation attorneys / notary public; registered with the Court of Registration
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: Certified copy from incorporation notary → Apostille by MOFA Korea → accepted in all Hague countries; Consular Legalization path for non-Hague jurisdictions: Korean notary certification → MOFA Korea authentication → consular section of the destination state in Seoul → final destination country authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (은행 거래 확인서 / 잔고 증명서) issued by a licensed Korean bank (e.g., Hana, Shinhan, Woori, KEB Hana, Kookmin)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: Bank officer signature → Korean notary public acknowledgment → Apostille by MOFA Korea → direct submission to receiving foreign bank; non-Hague consular legalization path: Bank letter → Korean MOFA authentication → Consular Office of receiving country in Korea → legalization in the destination country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory dual-layer screening at formation and before onboarding any shareholder, director, or beneficial owner. Layer 1: Automated name, date-of-birth, and passport match against OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HM Treasury Consolidated List, Korean FSC Financial Action Task Force non-cooperative jurisdictions list, and the Korean KFTC/KOFC comprehensive sanctions list. Layer 2: Enhanced continuous due diligence (CDD) for any individual identified as a Politically Exposed Person (PEP), family member, or known close associate under FATF Recommendation 12, including verification against the Korean Public Officials Election Act, the Act on the Prevention of Corruption and Bribery and the establishment of the Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission, and global PEP databases. For each new shareholder or transferee of any issued share, confirmation that the party is not a resident of, or funded by accounts controlled from, North Korea, Iran, Syria, Cuba, or Crimea/Sevastopol. Because underwriters and overseas correspondent banks will rely on the Korean corporate KYC package, all screening results must be documented, signed, and retained for at least five years under the Korean AML/CTF Act Article 4, with immediate suspicious transaction reports (STR) filed to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) within 24 hours if any adverse match is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Corporate Registration Online Search Service (인터넷등기소 / i-REGISTRY: https://www.iros.go.kr) and the Korean Trade/Company Name Preliminary Verification via the Korean Intellectual Property Office (KIPO) trademark database; final name registration by the Court of Registration at the local district court having jurisdiction over the registered head office
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Korean name must be in Hangul (한글) script, without spaces between brand tokens in the corporate legal name. A phonetic transliteration rule applies where any foreign-language component is combined with a Korean legal form suffix; the entity must be named exactly as '상호 + 주식회사' or 'Chusik Hoesa' in Korean domain. For English filing purposes, the legal name may be transliterated into romanized Korean standard (Revised Romanization of Korean, Ministry of Culture Standard, e.g., 'Hanguk'), but the statutory registered name is the Hangul script version recorded by the Court of Registration. Four-tier naming convention: (1) First tier: distinctive brand name in Hangul/foreign transliteration; (2) Second tier: business descriptive element (e.g., '로지스틱스', '디스패치', '플릿', '텔레매틱스'); (3) Third tier: optional business classification (e.g., '소프트웨어', '컨설팅'); (4) Fourth tier: mandatory legal form suffix '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa). The name must be distinguishable from all pre-existing registered trademarks and corporate registrations, and must not be identical or confusingly similar to an existing Korean company name, trade name, or KIPO registered trademark.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: 은행 (bank), 보험 (insurance), 증권 (securities), 투자 (investment), 자산운용 (asset management), 대부 (loan), 신용 (credit), 카드 (card), 지급 (payment), 전자금융 (electronic finance), 금융 (financial), 저축 (savings), 신탁 (trust), 사채 (bond/brokerage), 국민 (national), 정부 (government), 대한민국 (Republic of Korea), 시 (city), 도 (province), 특별시 (special city), 광역시 (metropolitan city), 국가 (state), 경찰 (police), 검찰 (prosecution), 국방 (national defense), 군 (army/military), 중앙 (central), 한국은행 (Bank of Korea), 한국산업은행 (Korea Development Bank), 법원 (court), 헌법 (constitution), 선거 (election), 정당 (political party), 교황 (papal), 유엔 (UN), 나토 (NATO), 적십자 (Red Cross), 올림픽 (Olympic), 총장 (chancellor), 회계법인 (accountancy corporation), 법무법인 (law firm), 특허법인 (patent law firm), 감사 (audit), 의료 (medical), 병원 (hospital), 약국 (pharmacy), 학교 (school), 대학 (university), 학원 (private institute), 유치원 (kindergarten), 장의 (funeral), 장례 (funeral), 레미콘 (ready-mixed concrete), 택시 (taxi), 화물 (freight), and any token implying a regulated financial, defense, public authority, legal, medical, educational, or religious function without prior ministerial or district governor approval under the Commercial Act and the Act on Promotion of Corporate Name Usage.

Additional ministerial approval is required for any use of 'Korea' (한국), 'Republic of Korea' (대한민국), 'Seoul' (서울) or other local government names, 'National' (국가/국민), 'Bank' (은행), 'Securities' (증권), 'Insurance' (보험), and any token suggesting financial investment business or regulated peer-to-peer lending under the Act on Registration of Credit Business and Protection of Finance Users.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a name rejection, the applicant or its Korean legal counsel must first obtain the written or electronic rejection reason from the i-REGISTRY screen and the respective district court registration officer. Within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, counsel must file a formal administrative appeal under Article 292(2) of the Korean Commercial Act and the Rules on Registration of Commercial Names with the head of the relevant district court, using Form 제21호. The appeal submission must include the proposed name again, an explanation of how it satisfies the distinctiveness requirement under Article 23 of the Commercial Act and Article 43(1) of the Commercial Registration Rules, a comparative list of at least five existing Korean registrations (if any) that share the same descriptive token, and proof that the proposed name does not falsely imply a regulated financial, governmental, or educational function, and, where sensitive tokens are involved, the prior ministerial approval letter from the relevant competent authority (e.g., Financial Services Commission for financial terms). The district court must rule within 30 days; if the court rejects, the applicant may file a subsequent objection to the appellate court (항고) within 14 days from receipt, attaching a Korean patent/trademark attorney and Korean counsel argument on confusion likelihood, phonetics, and common law or statutory trade-name protectability. The appeal procedure is free of filing tax, but legal service fees of between KRW 1,500,000 and KRW 3,500,000 typically apply, and the total cycle time should be assumed as 30-50 calendar days before a any revised name can be processed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office or commercial mail-forwarding addresses are generally permissible to physically register a Korean Chusik Hoesa only if they are provided by a licensed corporate service provider with a real lease and a designated office room or dedicated cubicle that the company can access on short notice, but the National Tax Service and the local tax office (세무서) increasingly reject business addresses that are merely commercial mailboxes or that are shared by more than a threshold number of registered companies without separate signage or a dedicated workspace. For a B2B SaaS logistics telematics company targeting Stripe Billing and wire transfer payment rails, the address will be assessed for economic substance under the Korean tax law doctrine of 'place of effective management' and the requirement to maintain books, records, and physical server/backup infrastructure at the registered address if VAT invoices are issued. A virtual office that includes a physical presence service, mail forwarding, a registered agent, a local director attendance room, and a separate lease in the same building will be accepted, but a pure PO-box or digital mailbox is unacceptable to Korean banks during KYC. To satisfy the Korea Economic Substance Notification and foreign bank account opening requirements, the company should maintain a full-time or part-time registered employee at the address if the enterprise is deemed a 'limited, low-risk logistics SaaS' under the Korean AML risk-tier; otherwise, the bank may request additional business invoices. Quantified risk: if the registered address is a virtual office without an actual employee or desk, the probability of the relevant local tax office requesting documentary evidence, a phone inspection, or excise visit is approximately 50% to 70% within the first fiscal year.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) municipal or local tax office officials may conduct unannounced on-site verification (현지확인) of the registered head office if the company issues a high volume of tax invoices without matching office infrastructure; (2) district court registration personnel rarely inspect, but the National Tax Service (NTS) may inspect when the business type is 'software development and supply' with cross-border wire receiving patterns; (3) Korean Customs and the Korea Internet & Security Agency (KISA) may request network infra details for telematics data processing; (4) AML compliance imposes a requirement that the registered agent's office provide visitor logs and a physical document archive. Overall quantified likelihood: for a single-member (non-resident majority) Chusik Hoesa, unannounced on-site inspection by the NTS during the pre-incorporation and first fiscal year is estimated at approximately 20% to 35% (moderate), rising sharply if the entity uses a shared coworking mailbox, has no local employee, or requests VAT refunds. Proactive mitigation: place a discreet but visible sign, maintain a properly furnished office, preserve the lease certificate, and register the address with the local district as a 'business place of employment'.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: The Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, particularly Articles 289, 291, 293, 295, 317 and 391, as amended by the Korean Commercial Code reforms, together with the Registration of Corporate Naming and the Certified Public Notary Act as applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court within whose territorial jurisdiction the registered office is located; for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (Chusik Hoesa)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under the amended Commercial Act, a Chusik Hoesa may be incorporated with no statutory minimum paid-in capital. However, all subscribed shares must be fully paid up before registration, and the payment must be made into a Korean financial institution capital deposit account. There is no legal blocked escrow account requirement for the export-oriented logistics technology business described in this file.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY], A CHUSIK HOESA ORGANIZED UNDER THE COMMERCIAL ACT OF THE REPUBLIC OF KOREA. WHEREAS [COMPANY] was formed as a stock company under Articles 289, 295 and 317 of the Commercial Act; WHEREAS the incorporators have lawfully subscribed to the initial share capital and have fully paid the aggregate subscription price into the capital deposit account of the Company; and WHEREAS the first directors and statutory auditor have been duly elected at the inaugural general meeting of shareholders; NOW, THEREFORE, the directors, acting as the first board of directors, approve the following resolutions by unanimous written consent. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONFIRMATION: RESOLVED, that the board records and ratifies the subscription list and confirms that the issued share capital of [NUMBER] ordinary shares with a par value of [AMOUNT] Korean Won per share has been validly subscribed, allotted and fully paid in cash, and that the capital payment certificate issued by [BANK] shall be delivered to the registration officer. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company in the Republic of Korea is fixed at [ADDRESS], within the territorial jurisdiction of the [COURT] District Court, and that the chief executive officer is authorized to execute, notarize and deliver the lease, owner consents and utility authorizations necessary to establish such registered office. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Company shall open and maintain corporate bank accounts with [BANK]; and the representative director, together with one other authorized signatory, is authorized to execute account opening forms, wire transfer instructions, checks, payment orders and online banking agreements in the name of the Company, subject to the convenience and safe custody requirements of the board. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that [NAME] is appointed as Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director, [NAME] is appointed as Chief Financial Officer and Director, and [NAME] is appointed as Statutory Auditor of the Company, all such appointments to take effect immediately and to continue until the next annual general meeting of shareholders or earlier vacation of office. 5. FILING AND REGISTRATION AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the Representative Director is authorized to prepare, sign, submit and, if necessary, notarize the incorporation registration application to the competent District Court Registration Division, to pay registration taxes and fees, to obtain the official corporate seal and to take all lawful steps required to complete the statutory formation of the Company. 6. GOVERNANCE AND LEGAL EFFECT: RESOLVED, that all actions taken by the directors, officers and agents of the Company in connection with the formation, banking and licensing arrangements described above are ratified, confirmed and approved in all respects, and that this written resolution remains binding on the Company and its shareholders until amended by a qualified board resolution. This resolution is executed and effective as of the date written below.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation, Subscription and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Korean Notary Public and the Company's registered legal counsel; no court filing at this pre-incorporation stage
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: We recommend that the founders first select a unique corporate name and verify that no identical Korean name is registered on the name search system maintained by the courts. The articles of incorporation must state the corporate purpose, the names of the founders, the total number of shares to be issued, the par value, the place of the registered office, the method of public notice, and the initial directors. The articles must be signed or sealed by every incorporator and notarized by a notary. The incorporators shall then execute share subscription applications and appoint the first directors and auditor. All documents should be prepared in bilingual format if any director is a non-resident, and passports must be certified.
required_dossiers: certificates of passport of each foreign incorporator or director
written consents of first directors and auditor
registered office address and landlord consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a request for cure, amend the defective articles and have them re-executed; if the name search conflicts, choose a new corporate name and update the articles before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Capital Deposit Account and Payment of Share Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A Korean commercial bank licensed under the Banking Act, selected as the deposit bank under the Commercial Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The incorporators shall open a temporary capital deposit account in the name of the proposed company or of the incorporators with the selected bank. The full subscription moneys must be deposited before the application for incorporation registration is submitted. The bank will issue a capital payment deposit certificate confirming the amount paid and the account details. The incorporators must store the certificate in the company file because the registration officer will require proof of payment. If the share capital is paid by a corporate parent, a board resolution of the parent authorizing the remittance must be kept. No escrow release will be required, but for foreign exchange compliance the payment must be declared and reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; if foreign investment protection is desired, the investment should also be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
required_dossiers: remittance instruction with source of funds declaration
capital payment deposit certificate from the bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank delays due to anti-money laundering verification, provide beneficial ownership declarations and source-of-funds records; if payment is returned, repay into the same account or select another licensed bank and obtain a fresh certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Registration to the District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division, Seoul Central District Court or local District Court in which the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: No later than two weeks after the capital contribution is completed, the representative director must prepare and submit the application for registration of incorporation to the registry office having jurisdiction over the registered office. The applicant must file the notarized articles, the capital deposit certificate, the incorporators report, the written appointment and acceptance of the directors and auditor, and the identity proof of incorporators if they are natural persons. The registration officer verifies that all mandatory statutory requirements are met and then records the company in the commercial register and issues a certificate of registered matters. The company comes into existence as a legal person upon such registration. Registration tax is calculated based on paid-in capital, and local education surtax is assessed at the prevailing rate.
required_dossiers: application for stock company incorporation registration
capital deposit certificate or payment report
consent or acceptance letters of directors and auditor
identification documents of directors and incorporators
power of attorney if filed by counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a supplementary order, supply the missing documents within the statutory supplementary period, usually 14 days; if the application is suspended for a formal defect, file a corrected application with the same registry; if rejected, the applicant may apply for reconsideration and then an immediate appeal to the district court within eight days of notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate and Business Tax Registration with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea, through the local District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered office or through the Home Tax service portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of registration of incorporation, the company must file corporate tax registration and, if the company engages in a value-added taxable business, apply for a business registration certificate. The application must include the certified copy of the commercial register, the company articles, the representative director identification, the lease agreement for the registered office, and the corporate bank account certificate. The National Tax Service will issue the business registration number and the electronic tax invoice authentication certificate. For a software or logistics technology company that will issue invoices to domestic Korean customers, VAT registration is a critical step; for cross-border export services, export tax invoices may be handled under the VAT Act. The finance director should also register the company for tax accounting and payroll withholding if it will employ staff.
required_dossiers: certificate of corporate registration issued by court registry
representative director passport or national ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service requests clarification of the business purpose, submit the ISIC description and a brief business plan within seven days; if the registration is rejected, visit the local tax office with the original supporting dossiers; if the delay exceeds the statutory timeline, request a certificate of non-filing and appeal to the Regional Tax Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Regulatory Assessment for Fleet Telematics Software and Optional Location Information Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Communications Commission and Personal Information Protection Commission; no local industrial license if no physical facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Given the ISIC 6201 code and logistics fleet dispatch platform, the company must determine whether its real-time telematics processing establishes a location information business requiring a license under the Location Information Act and prior consent under the Personal Information Protection Act. If the platform uses location data for navigation, dispatch, or fleet-risk scoring, a location information permission from the Korea Communications Commission may be necessary. If the service merely aggregates externally provided telematics data without processing personal location, no such permission is required. This step also confirms that no ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly or warehousing operation is being commenced, and therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment, Civil Defense fire permit, warehouse operating license or manufacturing facility license is triggered.
required_dossiers: service architecture and data flow description
corporate registration and business registration certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a regulator determines that location information processing is reportable, submit the location information business registration application with the identified dossiers; if the regulator issues a corrective order under the Personal Information Protection Act, implement the required technical or contractual controls within fifteen days and file a compliance statement; if the application is queried, supply a legal memorandum with the regulator and request an extension.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable. The only potential authority for data-location authorization is the Korea Communications Commission, but the current logistics SaaS model does not require an industrial operating license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable. No industrial operation license is required for ISIC 6201 computer programming and related activities as structured.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea - Not Applicable for pure digital services
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt. ISIC 6201 is a service activity not listed in the mandatory EIA Act positive schedules and no physical development site is involved.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. No industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste generation at the registered office. Information-technology equipment should be recycled through a licensed e-waste collector under the Waste Management Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable as an industrial license. The building owner must maintain fire-fighting installations and structural safety inspections under the Firefighting System Installation and Maintenance Act. Before employees occupy the office, a fire safety inspection confirmation should be obtained from the district fire department. No separate Civil Defense permit is required for software offices. If the company employs five or more workers, it must report the workplace to the Ministry of Employment and Labor for occupational safety and health registration.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea, operating through the HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); Korea Customs Service (KCS) for border/customs export declaration administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity that, like the Chusik Hoesa, establishes a domestic corporation or a domestic place of business in the Republic of Korea must first complete Commercial Act incorporation or foreign branch registration, then file a corporate business registration application (Business Registration Certificate application) with the district tax office having jurisdiction over the registered head office or domestic place of business. The application should be submitted through the South Korean company registration system or HomeTax within the statutory period, generally within two months of incorporation or commencement of business. Upon acceptance, the NTS issues the 10-digit Korean Tax Number and Corporate Business Registration Number, which jointly serve as the corporate TIN and VAT registration number. If the foreign entity has no domestic place of business but is required to file Korean VAT on electronic services supplied to Korean consumers, it must register as a foreign electronic service supplier directly through HomeTax and receive a VAT registration number before commencing taxable supplies. A foreign corporation without a domestic establishment that only earns Korean-source investment income is instead registered in the NTS foreign non-resident taxpayer register rather than under the business-registration regime, and corporate tax is collected through withholding where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (the Chusik Hoesa is treated as a Korean domestic corporation, separately taxable on worldwide income under the Corporate Tax Act; it is not pass-through, and there is no general entity-classification election for U.S.-style check-the-box treatment).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean tax law does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity election. Once incorporated as a Chusik Hoesa, the entity is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation for corporate tax and VAT purposes. No elective transparent treatment is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act (VAT Act), administered by the National Tax Service
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 registration threshold for legal entities: a Chusik Hoesa or any corporation supplying goods or services in Korea must register as a general VAT taxpayer before commencement regardless of turnover. For individuals only, simplified taxable person status may apply when the prior-year taxable turnover is KRW 30 million or less; this simplified regime is unavailable to corporations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All registered VAT businesses must issue tax invoices for taxable supplies to other VAT-registered businesses. Under the mandatory e-tax invoice regime, tax invoices must be transmitted electronically to the NTS through the HomeTax portal or an NTS-approved electronic tax invoice service provider. The NTS clears each e-tax invoice into its central invoice database and performs cross-matching among issuers, recipients, cash-receipt data and periodic VAT returns. There is no physical anti-fraud stamp; integrity is enforced through mandatory transmission of encrypted electronic invoice XML, sequential invoice-number controls, and NTS transaction monitoring for mismatches and false invoices. Cash sales to individuals must also be reported through the HomeTax cash-receipt system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Korean VAT Act, zero-rating applies to exported goods, services supplied outside Korea, and certain services provided to non-residents in foreign currency. For the fleet-telematics SaaS and ISIC 6201 activity, the zero rate may be claimed where the place of supply is outside Korea, meaning the foreign customer receives or uses the software and real-time telematics services outside Korea, and the supply is made to a non-resident counterparty. If the supply is instead treated as supplied to a Korean customer or consumed by a fixed establishment in Korea, standard 10% VAT applies. The supporting position must be evidenced by commercial documentation, technology or service-usage records, and foreign-exchange receipts.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration (Export Declaration Certificate or electronically transmitted export declaration) for goods; for services, a substitute document package is required
Commercial invoice and executed service agreement stating the non-resident customer, the nature of the SaaS and telematics service, and the place of use outside Korea
Proof of export or delivery: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for physical goods; for services, server or service-use logs, or a signed statement from the foreign customer confirming use outside Korea

Foreign exchange repatriation evidence: a Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate or certified Foreign Remittance Receipt from a Korean designated foreign exchange bank showing receipt of export proceeds in convertible foreign currency
HomeTax export-settlement reporting input matching the invoice amount, customer name and date of payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service scrutinize zero-rated export claims by matching VAT return e-invoice data, customs export declarations, bank non-resident remittance records and service-consumption evidence. If zero-rating is denied because the documentation is incomplete, the supplies are not actually exported, or the service is found to be consumed in Korea, the NTS will assess unpaid VAT at 10% retrospectively, impose an unfaithful-return additional tax of up to 40% of the underpaid VAT, and charge statutory late-payment interest from the original filing due date. False or fraudulent export evidence can lead to tax evasion investigation under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, clawback over the 10-year fraudulent-assessment limitation period, and criminal liability. Immediate reversal of any input-VAT refund previously claimed on the export cost base will also be required.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, acting as executor and supervisory authority for the Ministry of Economy and Finance under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA) and Foreign Exchange Business Regulations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a broadly open but regulated foreign exchange system. The Korean won is freely convertible on the current account for genuine trade, service, royalty, and dividend flows, provided the underlying transaction is declared through a reporting institution (a licensed foreign exchange bank). Capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment, cross-border loans, and equity subscriptions, are liberalised but require formal filings and may be subject to ad hoc restrictions when market volatility creates national emergency. For a Chusik Hoesa engaged in logistics SaaS, the practical constraint is the need to prove the 'real business purpose' of every substantial cross-border flow. Dividends and profit remittances to foreign shareholders require cumulative investment registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, a certified dividend resolution, and proof of non-resident tax withholding paid to the National Tax Service. The bank will also review that the original capital entered via an inbound foreign direct investment route under a proper purpose code; if the share capital was funnelled through an offshore account or a third-country intermediary without sequential payment, the withdrawal path will be blocked. Periodic BOK statistics reporting applies to foreign exchange positions above certain thresholds, and Korean banks enforce strict anti-fragmentation rules to detect round-tripping. Overall, current account convertibility is unrestricted, while capital account freedoms demand documentary diligence rather than monetary restriction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the FETA and the enforcement decrees on exports, export proceeds from software, telematics, and fleet-dispatch services must be received within twelve months from the export declaration or invoice date; the period is extendable by up to eighteen months with prior Bank of Korea approval or where a recognised foreign exchange bank has been notified. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to Korean won for private commercial exporters; the Chusik Hoesa may retain 100% of export receipts in Korean won onshore foreign-currency current accounts. However, every collection must be remitted into a domestic foreign-exchange bank account and reported in the Electronic Export Ledger; any deviation is treated as an unapproved disposal and can trigger cancelation of trade entitlements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Current Account / Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Direct Investment
Operational Currency Account (KRW & USD) with Export Proceeds Ledger
Capital Verification Escrow Account and Operational Trading Account
Non-Resident Investment Account / Full-Service Treasury Account
Agricultural and SME Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability for any non-Korean fintech EMI or offshore digital e-money institution. The Chusik Hoesa cannot legally maintain treasury or settlement accounts with EMI licensees that are not recognized foreign exchange banks under the FETA. Offshore EMIs are barred from opening multi-currency corporate accounts in South Korea, and they are not permitted to execute foreign exchange payment orders on behalf of a Korean resident entity. Even domestic-tier online banking platforms such as Toss or Kakaobank cannot serve as the primary FX clearing bank because they lack the full delegated authority to assign BOK foreign exchange purpose codes and to issue foreign-investment certificates. Consequently, the treasury blueprint must centralise all cross-border liquidity through the tier-1 banks; EMIs can only be used as invoicing or API middleware, never as the regulated clearing rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa with a non-resident shareholder or foreign statutory director, the beneficiary bank requires a physical in-branch appearance by at least one authorised signatory and the compliance-committee member at account activation. The consular proxy opening path is not recognised for the commercial operational account; the director may prepare the full package through the Korean Notary Act and issue a power of attorney, but the designated representative must still attend a live interview at the branch, either in Seoul or another banking centre, before the account number is released. For remote overseas directors, a video interview may be used only after the bank has collected notarised and apostilled incorporations, and it still demands a second local KYC attender in many branches. For the initial capital escrow account, the Korean foreign-investment broker or law firm can act under a limited POA to open the account, but the final operational account mandates direct director presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign beneficial owner with high-risk jurisdiction exposure and a multi-layered offshore shareholding structure in the Chusik Hoesa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete verified ownership chain from ultimate natural persons down to the corporate share register; certified copies of passport and alien registration; notarised statements of wealth with source-of-wealth letters; historical 3-year tax filings from the foreign shareholder; bank reference letters from the originating offshore banks; and a full corporate registry extract with audited financial statements for each intermediate entity, supported by a legal opinion from a Korean counsel confirming compliance with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the nominal business scope (software development) and the technical service description (fleet telematics and dispatch), which can trigger a 'fictitious trade' red flag
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master services agreements with at least three logistics operators in the Asia-Pacific region; product and telematics system documentation; server hosting certificates in South Korea; screen captures of the live dispatch dashboard; standard lease or licensing contracts for the fleet hardware; an independent audit of the code repository and database structure; and a detailed corporate brochure on the fleet route-optimisation solution, all accompanied by customer acknowledgements of service delivery.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and export-control nexus: use of vessel or vehicle tracking that may inadvertently cover blacklisted ports, air routes, or illegally designated enterprises
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A documented know-your-client procurement policy restricting access to the fleet platform to non-sanctioned jurisdictions; an up-to-date denied-party-screening report from OFAC, EU, and Korean KFTC lists covering all counter-parties; a signed no-transshipment and no-sanctuary certificate; an IMO or VIN registry evidence for each fleet unit; and a monthly audit log of the anti-circumvention screening performed through the platform.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital verification concerns: initial capital remitted from a third-country financial account instead of the ultimate shareholder's bank account, with mixed source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreement and share register for the Chusik Hoesa; a certified 'Certificate of Foreign Currency Acquisition' issued by the Korean foreign exchange bank; the underlying remittance SWIFT MT103 message header showing the originating bank and route; a bank confirmation letter proving the USD or KRW deposit rate used at the time of investment; a written explanation and documentary proof of the third-country vehicle's purpose (e.g., treasury planning, royalty pooling, or venture capital holding), supplemented by the vehicle's statutory audit report and a statement from the Korean licensed certified accountant that the capital contribution matches the statutory books.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity subscription must be routed from the ultimate shareholder's bank account directly to the foreign exchange bank that will issue the Foreign Investment Certificate, with a SWIFT MT103/200 message including the phrase 'FIPA - Foreign Direct Investment' and the appropriate BOK purpose code for capital investment (e.g. article 18, type 101). The routing cannot pass through a personal account or a foreign EMI. The bank verifies the currency transfer against the incorporation documents, then files the foreign direct investment report with the Ministry of Economy and Finance through the tax office. Within twenty banking days, the Chusik Hoesa receives a capital verification certificate, which enables the account to be converted from a full reserve or escrow status to an operational current account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For operational procurement of vehicles, telematics equipment, and overseas cloud infrastructure, the Chusik Hoesa should execute outbound settlement through (a) SWIFT MT103 wire transfers for software licensing fees and maritime or roadway dispatcher subscriptions; (b) documentary collections (DP/DA) for low-value fleet hardware; and (c) irrevocable confirmable letters of credit (LOC) for high-value purchases of vehicle tracker units. All outbound payments above KRW 500,000,000 equivalent must be reported to the Bank of Korea through the bank's electronic reporting system. The reimbursements for logistics dispatch invoices from Korean carriers must be received as domestic wire transfers into the KRW operating account, while cross-border license fees into the foreign currency account are enforced with the commercial invoice and the transport disposition documents.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable KRW/USD onshore forward contracts up to twelve months, documented with a valid import/export contract or sevice-deal underlying exposure

KRW/USD non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts permitted only with a non-resident counterparty and on a non-deliverable KRW basis; onshore residents are prohibited from using NDFs for disguised speculation

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CRS) where both legs are directly linked to confirmed long-term contracts in logistics software and fleet leasing; the swap notional must not exceed the anticipated net cash flow and must be submitted to the foreign exchange bank for approval
Zero-premium structured collars or participating forwards allowed only when executed through the tier-1 bank's dealing desk and strictly recorded as trade-related hedge instruments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Financial Statement Attachments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month following fiscal year-end; March 31 for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of up to 20% of unpaid tax for late or omitted filing plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest; continued delinquency permits NTS asset seizure and cancellation of business registration. No judicial administrative strike-off applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surcharge Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government through the NTS one-stop corporate tax filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same statutory window as the central corporate income tax return; March 31 for a calendar-year company.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted local surcharge filing triggers a 20% penalty on the unpaid local tax and daily late-payment interest, followed by local-government enforcement measures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting and Board Resolution Record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate minute book; court registration office only where directors or officers change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary shareholders' meeting no later than March 31 for calendar-year companies; board resolutions recorded in the minute book at the same meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may face Commercial Act penalty provisions if the annual meeting is not convened; late commercial registry filings for officer changes trigger late-filing penalties and registration tax surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Externally Audited Financial Statements and Auditor's Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For companies subject to external audit, audited statements are approved at the annual shareholders' meeting and then filed on DART immediately after approval; the annual meeting must occur by March 31 for calendar-year companies.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to disclose on DART triggers FSS administrative enforcement and fines; failure to appoint a required external auditor subjects the company to regulator-imposed auditor designation and penalty surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Shareholder Ledger Annual Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company's statutory register inspected at the registered office; no public central-UBO filing for a private Chusik Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the annual shareholders' meeting and updated on each share transfer; for calendar-year companies, reconciled by March 31.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of a current shareholder ledger is a Commercial Act documentation violation and an AML deficiency; banks may withdraw payment-rail access and tax authorities may challenge shareholder-based tax attributes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external audit applies to a Chusik Hoesa with total assets of KRW 12 billion or more at fiscal year-end; listed companies and certain large unlisted companies are separately captured. A logistics-technology SaaS company below the threshold is exempt but may elect an audit for shareholder or lender comfort.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS for listed and public-interest entities; a private Chusik Hoesa may present standalone accounts under K-GAAP with K-IFRS permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require a private Chusik Hoesa to file an annual UBO return with a central statutory register. The company must maintain a current register of members and, for AML/KYC, financial institutions must verify beneficial-owner data at least annually and upon substantive shareholding changes. Disclosure to the tax authority occurs through the corporate tax return and foreign-investment filings, not as a standalone annual UBO form.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Board of Directors Meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 1,500 per year for a professional Seoul registered-office and corporate secretarial arrangement
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - 25,000 for a small-to-mid-size Chusik Hoesa, dependent on asset complexity and consolidated group scale

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Progressive statutory rates of 9%, 19%, and 21% on taxable income brackets up to KRW 200 million, KRW 20 billion, and over KRW 20 billion respectively; 25% headline rate applicable only to the portion exceeding KRW 300 billion. Eligible logistics-tech SaaS companies may claim the R&D tax credit (up to 30–40% of qualifying R&D costs), technology business income deduction (50% deduction for 7 years), and the Global Business Income deduction for foreign-invested high-tech businesses.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: National Tax Service (NTS) HomeTax electronic filing system — Corporate Tax Return Form No. 1105
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year-end December 31: file by April 30 of the following year (within 4 months of fiscal year-end). For other fiscal year-ends, the deadline is 4 months after that fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: corporate name, business registration number, tax office code, fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations file using their domestic place of business (PE) registration number and must identify the foreign head office in supplementary declarations
Korean-source income attributable to the domestic PE only; foreign-source income reported in separate schedules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses: cost of sales, wages, utilities, depreciation, rent, business development, subcontracting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible only if properly documented with tax invoices and directly supporting the PE's Korean business activities

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible adjustments, tax-exempt income, and income deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reserve for PE remittance tax; non-deductible head office overhead allocations exceeding arm's length limits

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation after loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforward limited to 5 years; attributable to PE only if books and records properly maintained

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate tax computed at progressive rates
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply same progressive rates to the PE's taxable income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits and reduced tax rates (special taxation promoters)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE can claim statutory credits only if available under domestic law and treaty non-discrimination provisions

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Local income tax (10% surcharge on corporate tax)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE subject to identical local surcharge
Include quarterly interim prepayments and withheld tax credits; non-resident without a PE uses final withholding procedure

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of 0.75% per day on unpaid tax up to 36 months; unfaithful return penalty of 10% (negligent), 20% (failure to file), 40% (fraud); additional 25% penalty for non-payment by deadline; fines up to KRW 10 million for failure to provide supporting documentation in audits.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Non-resident shareholder must submit to the Korean withholding agent before dividend payment: (a) Application for Certificate of Resident Status, (b) Transaction-specific reduced rate form, (c) original Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the home tax authority, apostilled/legalized where required. Withholding agent files with district tax office via HomeTax. If relief not applied before payment, shareholder may claim refund within 3 years by filing a corrected return with the district tax office. Treaty relief is denied where the beneficial ownership test fails or the transaction lacks principal purpose / substance under GAAR and OECD Principal Purpose Test.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 20% plus 2% local surcharge (effective 22%); reduced treaty rates generally 10–15% for software / IP royalties. Interest: statutory 20% plus 2% local surcharge (effective 22%); treaty rate generally 10%, subject to beneficial ownership and LOB/PPT limitations.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: KRW 100 billion annual revenue triggers mandatory Local File and Master File preparation; KRW 50 billion in cross-border intercompany transactions triggers annual information return disclosure.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain separate ESR for domestic law, but substance over form, beneficial ownership, and OECD Pillar Two anti-avoidance rules apply. A Korean Chusik Hoesa must maintain substantive operations: office, employees, contracts, decision-making, and actual B2B SaaS dispatch activity in Korea.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Fabricating expenses, suppressing revenues, using fake paper invoices for logistics dispatch services, or shifting profits to shell foreign companies
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act: imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to 10 times the evaded tax; administrative 40% penalty; public disclosure as a serial tax evader
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors cannot hide behind corporate veil: civil joint and several liability for corporate tax, criminal imprisonment, travel bans, and personal asset seizure

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Utilizing tax-haven holding companies lacking economic substance to claim treaty benefits on dividend royalty streams
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty relief; 40% penalty; recharacterization under substance-over-form; retroactive assessment up to 5 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved transaction structure subject to personal liability for penalties and collusion-based criminal sanction

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare / submit Local File, Master File, or transaction-specific benchmarking reports for intercompany SaaS license fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty up to KRW 10 million per missing document; adjustment of taxable income with 10–30% additional tax; possible criminal referral if intentional misstatement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors secondarily liable under Corporate Income Tax Act; penalties may be collected personally

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Substance Failure (DTA Benefit Claim)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Claiming reduced tax rate while no actual economic activity exists in Korea — no board minutes, no employees, no operational substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of DTA benefit; full 22% withholding; penalties 40% of unpaid tax; cancellation of tax benefits retroactively
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors personally liable for unpaid withholding and subject to criminal penalty if found to have used shell to evade tax

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repatriating dividends or royalties through unauthorized foreign accounts without reporting under Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; structuring payments to avoid beneficial ownership disclosures
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to KRW 200 million for unreported FX transactions; AML penalties under Financial Transactions Reports Act — imprisonment up to 5 years or fine up to KRW 50 million, or both
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers criminally liable for AML violations; travel bans and extradition; personal restitution of foreign assets
